html:
Stećci are large carved stone tombstones made from the late 1100s to the 1500s across Bosnia and Herzegovina and nearby parts of Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro. About 70,000 survive, most of them in Bosnia.

They take the shape of slabs, chests and gabled houses, and many are decorated with scenes of hunting, dancing and tournaments, spirals, vines and crosses, with some inscriptions in Bosnian Cyrillic. They were used by Catholics, Orthodox and followers of the Bosnian Church alike, and the custom outlasted the Ottoman conquest for a time. The necropolis at Radimlja near Stolac is among the best known. In 2016 the stećci were listed as a World Heritage Site.
